items.action: Riverside municipalities restored some larger boats as living museum pieces, raising awareness of their historical and cultural value.
Associations and local authorities on both banks now hold regattas, gatherings, traditional painting workshops and boat-model exhibitions to celebrate traditional vessels.
The Seixal Municipal Ecomuseum naval centre has a craft workshop that restores and builds boats to original models; larger boats run scheduled cultural and educational trips.
items.who: Núcleo Naval do Ecomuseu Municipal do Seixal

items.action: Visitors to Lisbon can take cruises on restored traditional boats adapted for tourism, with views of the city and south bank.
Before the bridge opened, boats carried people and goods and linked towns between Santarém and Cascais faster than other means.
The bridge over the Tagus was inaugurated.
Boats transshipped cargo between large ships and the port of Lisbon.
The river was the era's motorway, busy with varied craft: fragatas, varinos, faluas, cangueiros, botes, botes de fragata, botes de pinho, barcos de água acima, canoas and catraios.
items.boat: Fragatas, Varinos, Faluas, Cangueiros, Botes, Botes de Fraga

items.action: Flat-bottomed boats could sail close to shallow banks and travel farther upriver.
Smaller boats carried people and goods such as fresh produce and groceries.
Cangueiros hauled heavy cargo including building materials, sand, stone and pine to fuel Lisbon's bread ovens.
items.cargo: building materials, sand, stone, pine for bread ovens

items.action: Faluas formed a fairly regular network carrying passengers; a children's rhyme about a falua from Belém survives.
Varinos, faluas and fragatas were the most decorated boats, with floral motifs and decorated lettering; each painter's style identified the boat's shipyard.
The colour sequence painted on the calcês, the upper mast, was mandatory in the register and identified a boat's origin and ownership.
Painting used bright red, blue, green, yellow and white chosen by painter or owner, without symbolism; pigment paints were later replaced by industrial paints.
Painters worked directly on the surface without preliminary drawing, except for symmetry, applying one colour at a time to all elements, with no precision instruments.
items.conditions: drawing only when symmetry was wanted

items.action: Studies and iconographic records such as paintings, engravings and photographs document life with the traditional Tagus boats and their people.
The most emotional records of life with the traditional boats and their crews are found in old Revue Theatre sketches and in fado lyrics about Lisbon and the Tagus.
A 1985 photograph shows the varino "O Boa Viagem", belonging to the Câmara Municipal da Moita.
